findings.claim: The new wrapper drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the current compilation. This includes diagnostics created with a null/Location.None location. Diagnostics previously reported with no location (e.g. via GetIdentifierLocation returning null on a metadata type, or null locations for parameters/constructors) were still delivered to users as project-level warnings. They are now silently suppressed. A user with a warning currently shown (or warnings-as-errors) will see it disappear, and a generic non-source diagnostic never surfaces.

receipt_plan.detail: Analyzer test: [MessagePackObject] type in the compiling assembly whose member references a type that yields a diagnostic with null/Location.None (e.g. a diagnostic built with GetIdentifierLocation/GetLocation returning null). Assert on base that the diagnostic is reported and on head that it is not.

findings.claim: Filtering applies to all diagnostics, including those on a type from a different compilation that has a MessagePackObject with a real problem (e.g. missing Key / both keys null, or invalid union) and is used by the compiling assembly. Previously those would be reported (at a location in another tree) or crash. Now they are dropped, so a user relying on the consuming assembly to report errors for a referenced type no longer sees them. The requirement only asked for no crash.

receipt_plan.detail: Two-compilation analyzer test: a referenced-assembly MessagePackObject with a member lacking [Key], used from the app. Compare diagnostics from base (reported) with head (suppressed).

findings.claim: The generator path may also pass a reportDiagnostic; the fix only guards the diagnostics sites changed. Other sites still index DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] (the issue mentions line 735 in addition to the two changed). If line 735 is reachable for metadata generic structs, the crash persists, so the requirement is not fully met.

receipt_plan.detail: Generator and analyzer tests with a two-project repro (generic struct Item<T> in referenced lib, used in app). Also try variants with a property with no key, a field member, and a ctor with no matching parameter, and assert there is no exception. Also grep for remaining DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] usages.
